THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Just as sharemarket prices are hitting an all-time high, corporate Australia is bracing for one of the most disappointing profit seasons in five years. In ann Australian Financial Review survey of 14 key industries, analysts and fund managers revealed many have alreay written off the December half and are pinning their full-year forecasts on a second-half recovery. Page 1.

Citibank is negotiating with accounting and management consulting firm Arthur Andersen to establish personal banking sites within Andersens' headquarters around the world in an attempt to attract wealthy customers. Page 1.

Ed McKelvey, of Wall Street investment house Goldman Sachs, claims America's economic expansion will not end in 1997 and could continue for many more years - a view shared by many economic analysts as the U.S. enters its seventh successive year of econoic growth. Page 1.

After more than a month of promoting their capital raisings, Austral Coal Ltd and Minyango Resources NL have failed to attract the institutional support they may have easily gained 12 months ago as institutions back off from the coal sector in response to the fall in prices. Page 17.

According to the latest InTech sector-performance survey for 1996, trustees of superannuation funds who want to hire investment managers to out-perform benchmarks should spend more time looking toward managers of overseas equity portfolios than managers of local securities. Page 17.

Crown Ltd has further acquired A$42.6 million from a share placement to institutional investors, intensifying the likelihood of the company to obtain the management rights of the Crown Casino in Melbourne from Lloyd Williams' Hudson Conway. . Page 18.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Industry experts are predicting that Australian and foreign banks may be forced to write off more than A$500 million in loans following the Wik decision on native title which may expose large areas of Australia to new legal challenges. The banks have been "caught out" on projects - including mines, gas pipelines and roads - which could be scrapped or delayed in coming months. Page 19.

A group of 50 major Australian companies have put their weight behind a massive "buy Australian" loyalty scheme. The campaign, Advantage Australia, involves organisations with combined sales of A$30 billion and will kick off with a A$10 million advertising blitz encouraging consumers to support Australian industry. Page 19.

Clothing retailer Just Jeans Holdings Ltd has cemented its push into New Zealand with the A$8.1 million takeover of Underground Fashions Ltd. The acquisition is designed to increase Just Jeans' turnover which was reported at A$340.5 million for the 12 months to July 27 last year. Page 20.

Canadian-based frozen food giant McCain Foods plans to spend at least another A$15 million this year on its Victorian and Tasmanian operations, in addition to the A$75 million spent over recent years, as the group increases its plans to use Australia as a food platform to Asia. Page 20.

Although Hunter Valley-based miner Cumnock Coal Ltd has achieved a 74 percent increase in production for the December quarter, it remains concerned that Japanese buyers of steaming coal may cut prices as producers wrap up annual price talks in Tokyo. Page 20.

Australian liquefied natural gas producers have been called upon to broaden their marketing appeal by the South Korean power industry which has indicated that it would be prepared to sign long-term contracts with the Woodside Petroleum Ltd-operated North est Shelf in Western Australia, to meet massive increases in power demand over the next decade. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Efforts to end a major pay TV dispute between The Seven Network and Optus Vision will intensify this week with Mayne Nickless - determined to sell its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications - planning to unveil a proposal aimed at breaking the deadlock between the warring parties and paving the way for the eventual stock exchange listing of Optus Communications. Page 25.

AWA has emerged as a strong competitor to take on Kerry Packer's bid to buy the NSW TAB from the state government. AWA is expected to make an offer of about A$750 million for 75 percent of NSW TAB with the remainder being earmarked for a sharemarket listing. Page 25.

Aussie Home Loans managing director John Symond has confirmed the group is finalising plans to expand its profit range in the wake of a tougher battle over home lending and will attack the banks in the credit card market and offer insurance products. Page 25.

Following British Telecom's moves to merge with American Telecommunications company MCI, the organisation has announced a possible link with Telstra as part of search for partners in the Asia-Pacific region. The link could range from and agreement for Teltra to distribute some of BT's advanced business products in Australia, to a joint venture, to Telstra buying into one of BT's companies. Page 27.

The rise of GIO shares from a low of A$3.17 to A$3.38, closing at A$3.31 on Friday, prompted GIO chief Bill Jocelyn to deny speculation he will stand down this year. Jocelyn also talked down market forecasts that the insurer's profits will get a boost from increased premiums. Page 27.

US-based Pacific Gas and Electricity has put a proposal to the Western Australia government for the development of a A$1 billion gas pipeline from Dampier to Collie which it believes will pave the way for huge industrial development of Western Australia's south-west. Page 27.
THE AGE

The National Australia Bank has secured a A$12 million licence for Mondex smart card technology in Asia, indicating the NAB is preparing to challenge the ANZ Bank's supremacy in Asia by offering retail banking products in carefully targeted markets. Page 1.

Just Jeans Holdings has launched a A$8 million takeover offer for the New Zealand-based fashion retailer and manufacturer Underground Fashions after reportedly coming to an agreement with the major stakeholders, the Risetto family, to buy their 70 percent holding in the popular women's wear retailer. Page C1.

Australia's three commercial television networks face pressure from dominant advertisers to slash advertising rates further in the second phase of the annual negotiation in which media buyers negotiate individual contracts on behalf of individual advertisrs. Page C2.

U.S. company Pacific Gas and Electricity has put forward a proposal to the Western Australian government to build a A$1 billion gas pipeline from Dampier to Collie in a move it believes will slash the cost of transporting gas from the North-West shelf to the south-west by about one-third. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
